messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: GPU memory errors observed on cluster gpu-pool-3. Severity: P1. Paging oncall anya.
anya: On it. I see repeated container restarts in prefill path for model 'redwood-13b-long'.
matt: Noted. Node metrics show VRAM spike just before restart, lots of long-context requests (>= 128k tokens) from a single customer key.
clara: Could be large prompt prefetch + KV cache blowout. Any CUDA traces?
anya: Pulling logs now.
anya: ``
[2026-03-17T03:21:12Z] runtime: CUDA error: out of memory (std::bad_alloc)
stack: runtime/allocator.cc:142 allocate -> inference/kv_cache.cc:78 reserve_prefix -> kernel.cu:301 launch_prefetch
Container restart: exit_code=137, reason=OOM
``
dave: Customer support flag: a subset of requests returned 503s between 03:20-03:27; impacted customers: acct-42 (high QPS) and acct-88.
leah: Temporal pattern looks like a burst from acct-42 rerunning a long-batch job. Could be noisy neighbor. Recommend immediate mitigation: temp throttle acct-42 and scale pool.
anya: Agreed. Action plan: 1) Apply rate-limit to acct-42 (burst reduction). 2) Drain offending pod and let scheduler move requests. 3) Fallback route: route long-window requests to small-window variant (redwood-13b-short) with warning. 4) Add emergency streaming trim (prefix trim) for >64k.
sanjay: I can push an autoscale bump (+2 GPUs) to gpu-pool-3, but may take ~3-5m. Doing now.
anya: @dave prepare a short customer note: "We observed elevated memory usage causing transient restarts for very long-context requests. We're applying throttles and fallbacks; brief errors possible. We will follow up with timeline."
dave: Drafted and posted to status: "Investigating GPU memory errors affecting long-context requests for a subset of customers. Mitigations in progress."
matt: Applied pod drain and forced eviction on the crashed container. Observed new pod scheduled to node node-27 but it's flagged with high allocation, scheduler placed on node-31 instead.
clara: Pushed a quick config change to enable prefix trimming at the runtime layer for requests with >64k tokens: ``config.runtime.max_prefill_tokens=65536; config.runtime.enable_prefix_trim=true``. This should reduce transient KV growth.
anya: Enabled the trim, monitoring metrics. VRAM usage for new pods dropping ~30%.
sanjay: Autoscale completed, +2 GPUs added to pool, new capacity online.
leah: After throttling acct-42 by 60% and enabling fallback routing for >64k, error rate dropped to baseline.
anya: Good. Customer impact: acct-42 saw ~40% requests 503s during the window, acct-88 had intermittent failures. No broader customer outage.
clara: Root cause hypothesis: unbounded prefetch/prefix population for extremely long contexts from a single key causing KV cache blowout and CUDA OOM. Need follow-ups: kernel-level guardrails and request-size protective limits in routing.
matt: Filed follow-up tickets: INF-4221 (runtime guardrails), INF-4222 (per-key soft-limits in gateway), INF-4223 (eviction policy improvements).
anya: Handoff to daytime oncall @leah for postmortem and customer comms. I'm tagging this as "mitigated". Will attach logs and timeline.
leah: Taking it. Will run a scrub runbook, collect traces, and confirm rollback safety for the prefix-trim flag.
dave: Customer update posted to acct-42 and acct-88. Support ticket numbers: SUP-9012, SUP-9013.
inc-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Playbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/gpu-memory-breach.
anya: Thanks team. Follow-ups: 1) short-term: keep prefix trim and per-key throttle for 24h. 2) mid-term: INF-4221/4222/4223. 3) long-term: capacity planning for long-window workloads and clearer SLAs on max context size.
clara: Adding perf metric alert: vram_utilization > 85% for 3m on any node => auto-throttle candidate.
leah: I'll coordinate postmortem and draft customer RCA. Closing pager for me once postmortem scheduled. :thumbsup:
